summaryReview.transcript: President Trump leaves today for a summit in Asia, and VR's Anthony Kuhn reports this summit will include an unprecedented three-way meeting Thursday with the leaders of Russia and China. Trump's first stop is Manila, the Philippines, where he will attend a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN. From there, it's on to the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Organization summit. Trump has said he wants to negotiate a new arms control deal with Russia and China, but China, which has the smallest nuclear arsenal of the three, is not likely to be interested. Trump will also try to extend a truce in the U.S.'s trade war with China. Trump's critics are concerned that Trump could side with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping in deciding the fate of smaller actors such as Ukraine and Taiwan without their participation or consent.
